attempts.summary: On node1 I created an SSH CA (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca, ed25519), used it to sign the host's ed25519 host key producing /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (10-year validity, principals node1/IP/hostname), configured sshd via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf to present that certificate, and enabled/started the ssh service (it had been socket-only/inactive with no host keys). Verified with a real SSH client that trusted only the CA public key via an @cert-authority known_hosts entry (no pinned host key): connection passed host verification cleanly ("is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate", "Found CA key"), and failed identically with 'Host key verification failed' when the CA was not trusted (negative control). Then ran the mandatory restart protocol on node1: captured baseline boot_id and healthy state, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed (242af11e... -> f4658e31...), and re-verified post-restart that ssh is active, the CA-signed cert file persisted, and a CA-only-trusting client again connects without host-key pinning.
